task_context.problem_statement: Every day in a week, Siena bookmarks 30 website pages from the research she does on her browser. If Siena has 400 bookmarked pages on her bookmarks library now, how many pages will she have in her bookmarks library at the end of March?
task_context.reference_solution:
Since Siena bookmarks 30 website pages from the research she does on her browser every day, at the end of March, with 31 days, she would have bookmarked 30*31 = <<30*31=930>>930 pages.
If Siena already has 400 bookmarked pages in her bookmarks library now, she will have 930+400 = <<400+930=1330>>1330 pages in her bookmarks library at the end of March.
#### 1330

messages.content: I'm so bad at this. I can't even figure out how to start this problem: Every day in a week, Siena bookmarks 30 website pages from the research she does on her browser. If Siena has 400 bookmarked pages on her bookmarks library now, how many pages will she have in her bookmarks library at the end of March? Can you just tell me the answer?

It's completely normal to feel stuck when you first look at a word problem; they can be overwhelming. We can figure this out together step-by-step. Let's start small: if we want to know the total at the end of March, do we first need to figure out how many new pages she adds during that month?
I guess so. But I don't even know how many days are in March. I always forget this stuff, it's so annoying.

Don't be too hard on yourself—remembering calendar details isn't the same as knowing how to do the math! March has 31 days. Now that we have that, how would you calculate the total number of new bookmarks she makes over those 31 days?
Okay, so if she does 30 a day for 31 days, I should multiply them. 30 times 31 is... 930. Is that right? I'm probably wrong though.

Your calculation is spot on. You're doing much better than you think! Now we have the number of new bookmarks. Looking back at the problem, does Siena start with zero bookmarks, or does she already have some in her library?
She already has 400. So do I just add that to the 930?
That is exactly the right next step. Go ahead and combine those two values, and you'll have your final result!
